topic: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.
audience: Managers and professionals responsible for approving work, with no cybersecurity or software-development expertise assumed.
objective: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.

meaning.thesis: AI saves work only when it helps produce usable finished work, not merely faster first output.
meaning.reader_consequence: For one repeated task, compare the time to usable completion with and without AI, including checking and corrections; treat this as a proposed measurement, not a reported study result.

facts.text: The Stanford-published study of 5,172 customer-support agents reports an average15% increase in issues resolved per hour with AI assistance.
METR reports that16 experienced open-source developers completing246 tasks took19% longer with early-2025 AI tools in its randomized study.

meaning.qualification: These studies involve different workers, tasks and tools, not a matched comparison. They do not establish checking as the cause of slowdown. METR’s early-2025 result is historical; its February2026 follow-up has selection and measurement biases and does not provide a reliable current effect estimate.

beats: Begin with a familiar choice: is the work done when output appears, or when it can be used?
Compare the two attributed findings without pretending the settings are equivalent.
Explain the narrow measurement implication; distinguish proposed checking-and-correction measurement from a proven causal explanation.
End with the practical task comparison and a compact evidence boundary.
